Before-Events

Intercept, modify, or cancel actions before they execute.

Overview

Before-events fire before the action executes, giving subscribers a chance to modify or cancel it. Two before-events exist: BeforeDamageEvent and BeforeHealEvent.

These are classes (not structs) so modifications persist. When a subscriber changes Amount or sets Cancel = true, those changes are visible to the Battle method that fired the event and to all subsequent subscribers.

BeforeDamageEvent

Fired by Battle.DealDamage() before any damage is applied.

Property Type Settable Description
Source ICombatant No The combatant dealing damage.
Target ICombatant No The combatant receiving damage.
Amount int Yes The damage amount. Modify this to increase or reduce damage.
DamageType string No Pass-through string for the type of damage (e.g. "Physical", "Magic").
Element string No Pass-through string for the element (e.g. "Fire", "Ice").
IsCrit bool No Whether this hit is a critical.
Cancel bool Yes Set to true to cancel the damage entirely. OnDamageDealt will not fire.

When Cancel is set to true, the damage is not applied and OnDamageDealt does not fire.

BeforeHealEvent

Fired by Battle.Heal() before any healing is applied.

Property Type Settable Description
Source ICombatant No The combatant performing the heal.
Target ICombatant No The combatant being healed.
Amount int Yes The heal amount. Modify this to boost or reduce healing.
Cancel bool Yes Set to true to cancel the heal entirely. OnHealed will not fire.

Same cancellation behavior as BeforeDamageEvent — when Cancel is true, the heal is not applied and OnHealed does not fire.

Example: Dodge System

Subscribe to OnBeforeDamage and cancel the event to implement a dodge mechanic:

battle.OnBeforeDamage += e =>
{
    // 20% dodge chance
    if (Random.value < 0.2f)
    {
        e.Cancel = true;
        Debug.Log($"{e.Target.Name} dodged the attack!");
    }
};

Example: Damage Reduction

Modify Amount to reduce incoming damage when a combatant is defending:

battle.OnBeforeDamage += e =>
{
    // Halve damage if target is defending
    if (IsDefending(e.Target))
        e.Amount /= 2;
};

Example: Healing Boost

Modify Amount on OnBeforeHeal to amplify healing:

battle.OnBeforeHeal += e =>
{
    // Double healing if healer has "Amplify" buff
    if (HasBuff(e.Source, "Amplify"))
        e.Amount *= 2;
};
Before-events are classes, not structs. This is intentional — modifications to Amount and Cancel must persist to the Battle method that fired the event. Multiple subscribers can all modify the same event.
